- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias; add 3–5% to prevent premature bottoming.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days trending down from peak), model should not overpredict continuation; adjust forecast to align with recent mean.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior day), model tends to overreact; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above prior high.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7) and price is volatile, reduce forecast volatility by smoothing 3–5 day moving average.  
- Forecast should not lag by more than 2–3 days relative to sentiment shift; if sentiment turns sharply, adjust forecast within 1–2 days to reflect new direction.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over 5+ days, model should not forecast upward unless confirmed by price action; treat as “low conviction” zone.  
- If forecast consistently exceeds true outcome by 3–5% over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 2–3% per day to correct for overconfidence bias.
